title: GPU OOM smoke tests and driver probes
content:
Purpose: quick, portable smoke tests + probing checklist for recurring GPU OOMs we see across cluster nodes. Intention is to produce a minimal repro and gather consistent telemetry across affected hosts before escalating to infra or driver vendor.

Summary of observed behavior:
- Symptoms: sudden process-level OOMs (CUDA out of memory) during long-running model inferences (token streaming). Some runs fail immediately, others after ~10-40k tokens. No obvious host memory exhaustion.
- Error snippets seen in user logs: "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.23 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 32.12 GiB already allocated; 7.75 GiB free; 1.42 GiB cached)" and intermittent driver traces: "E NVIDIA-SMI 515.48.07: failed to initialize NVML: Driver/library version mismatch"
- Affected fraction: ~3/28 nodes in GPU pool intermittently. Same model and container image runs fine on some nodes.

Quick triage checklist (what I run first)
- Reproduce baseline (same container + model): docker run --gpus all --rm \"/bin/bash -c 'python -u /app/serve.py --num-requests 200 --seq-len 2048'\" (run on both "good" and "bad" nodes)
- Monitor s-nap output: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,memory.total,memory.used,pstate,driver_version --format=csv -l 1 > /tmp/nvidia-stream.log &
- Capture kernel and driver: cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version; modinfo nvidia | sed -n '1,40p'
- Docker environment check: docker inspect --format='{{.Config.Env}}' <container_id> | grep -E 'LD_LIBRARY_PATH|CUDA_HOME|PATH'
- Host ldd of libs inside container: docker run --rm --entrypoint ldd <image> /usr/local/lib/python3.10/dist-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so | head -n 40

Commands I actually used and their rationale:
1) probe NVML init repeatedly: 
   for i in {1..10}; do nvidia-smi -q >/tmp/nsm_$i.txt; sleep 1; done
   - to catch intermittent NVML init failures (Driver/library mismatch shows up inconsistently)

2) check ldconfig / runtime mix: 
   strings /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so | head -n 5
   ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so |& grep -E 'libcuda|libcudart'
   - to ensure container isn't binding to host libcuda via LD_PRELOAD or wrong search path

3) check for co-located processes / stale contexts: 
   nvidia-smi pmon -i 0 -s um > /tmp/pmon.log & sleep 15; pkill -f pmon || true
   - occasionally an init process holds a large CUDA context and leaks memory across runs

4) collect complete Docker runtime info for node: sudo journalctl -u docker -S "-1h" | tail -n 200

Observed artifacts (examples copied from nodes)
- Node hostA: /proc/driver/nvidia/version -> "NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 525.85.12 Wed Jul 20 00:00:00 PDT 2025 NVRM..."
  nvidia-smi shows driver_version 525.85.12, but user container sees libcuda 525.60.11 (from /usr/local/cuda). Mismatch present.
- Node hostB: clean match (driver + libcuda both 525.85.12) and workloads stable.
- Node hostC: intermittent NVML init failures and occasional kernel oops in dmesg (soft lockups around NVMe not GPU).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Driver/library mismatch inside container (common): containers ship CUDA runtime libs that sometimes conflict with host driver; if libcuda symbols mismatch NVML init fails and can lead to bad memory accounting -> OOMs.
2) Allocation fragmentation / stale contexts: repeated small allocations and caching (torch.cuda.empty_cache semantics) cause fragmentation and eventual allocation failure even when total used < total capacity. Some older driver versions have worse fragmentation behavior.
3) Hidden host process holding persistent allocation (non-containerized process or system service) that is not visible to scheduler but consumes VRAM.
4) PCIe/NVLink partial failure causing reduced effective memory or erroneous reporting (less likely but possible on nodes with NVSwitch warnings).

Minimized repro plan (steps to collect deterministic trace)
- Step 0: snapshot environment: dpkg -l | grep -E 'nvidia|cuda' ; cat /etc/os-release ; uname -r ; pip freeze > /tmp/pip-freeze.txt
- Step 1: start a minimal container without shipping CUDA libs: docker run --rm --gpus all -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -e NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=compute,utility --entrypoint /bin/bash <image> -c "ldd /workspace/app/wheel/libsomething.so |& tee /tmp/ldd.txt; python /workspace/app/repro_minimal.py"
- Step 2: run with container volume mounting host /usr/lib/nvidia to force host libs: docker run --rm --gpus all -v /usr/lib/nvidia:/host_nvidia --entrypoint /bin/bash <image> -c "export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/host_nvidia:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH; python /workspace/app/repro_minimal.py"
- Step 3: if Step 2 stabilizes or destabilizes, record exact lib versions and compare. If mismatch confirmed, try starting container with --gpus all and environment variable NVIDIA_DISABLE_REQUIRE := 1 (not real, note: placeholder for vendor flags) to force pass through.

Repro script sketch (repro_minimal.py) - what I used to reproduce incremental leak:
- loop: alloc tensors of decreasing size until OOM, sleep 0.05, free some, track peak allocation via torch.cuda.memory_allocated() and torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated()
- record timestamped traces to /tmp/repro-trace.log with stack traces (faulthandler) on OOM

Telemetry to attach to Jira when escalating
- /var/log/syslog and dmesg snippets +/- 10 minutes of failure
- /tmp/nvidia-stream.log (nvidia-smi sampling at 1s) and pmon logs
- output of cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version and ldd outputs for libcuda/libcudart both inside container and on host
- container image id + Dockerfile snippet that copies /usr/local/cuda/lib64 into the image (if present)
- pip freeze inside image and kernel version

Short-term mitigations tried and results
- Rebooting node: temporary fix for ~24-48h (supports hypothesis of stale kernel module state)
- Forcing container to use host libs (bind-mount) in some cases made runs succeed (indicates shipped CUDA runtime mismatch)
- pinning image to use libcudart.so matching host driver (trial) reduced failure rate in a small canary (4->0 failures in 12h)

Longer-term actions / follow-ups
- Create a smoke-test that runs as a DaemonSet to detect driver/library mismatch on node boot: checks for NVML init, ldd of primary CUDA libs, and fails node if mismatch detected (run before scheduler accepts GPU pods).
- Add a pre-flight check in our container build pipeline to refuse baking host CUDA libs into user images (or at least warn).
- Investigate kernel upgrade plan: several failing nodes are 5.15.x whereas stable cluster nodes are 6.1.x; check vendor notes for driver 525 compatibility with 5.15 kernels.
- Work with infra to test updated NVIDIA driver (525.85.12 -> 530.x) on one pool (canary) to validate if fragmentation or NVML issues are mitigated.

Open questions / TODOs
- Why do some nodes show exact same driver/lib version but still fail? Need a capture of the full process list and open /dev/nvidia* handles during failure.
- Are there recent changes in our image build pipeline that copy CUDA runtime libs into app base images? Which commits? (trace: GH PRs with "cuda" files in Dockerfile: link above)
- If fragmentation: can we instrument allocator-level stats from Triton/PyTorch to prove fragmentation vs leak?

Notes to self: save this file as canonical user-facing debug steps. When I escalate put these artifacts into JIRA-ENG-8421 and tag infra and vendor.

Recent run notes (2026-03-11 22:18 UTC, hostA):
- repro_minimal.py: peak_alloc pattern: 6.1GB, 6.1GB, 12.2GB, 18.4GB, OOM at expected 19.0GB. nvidia-smi shows used: 18.8GB but free reported 21.2GB which doesn't add up vs program's view (torch reports 1.4GB free).
- Conclusion: mismatch between NVML and CUDA runtime bookkeeping likely due to library mismatch.

If you pick this up: run the reproducible plan on a "good" node first to validate script; then run the two-step container lib swap on a "bad" node and attach /tmp/* logs to linked Jira ticket.

-- Avery
